Text.Text: Bay One is cutting again and my paperwork finally matches my yard. That was your doing, so I'll say it once: the guard you carry now doesn't break, and neither does my word. There's a standing line on my roster with your name on it. Now stop blocking my light.
I can use a katar hand, but I won't hire an unfinished one for this. Reach rank 50 in Katar, then come back for the work order.

A wreck crew is cutting under my stamp without my permission. Six Adamantine Guard adepts hold the Breaker Bay on CZ-220. Put them down and bring me their work order. If my name's on it, I want to know who put it there.
I'll cut you a key. The maintenance level has the entrance to the Breaker Bay. Bring me that forged order and I can start taking my yard back.

Everything the galaxy is done with. Freighters, barge hulls, one decommissioned corvette I wasn't supposed to ask about. We cut it, sort it, weigh it, sell it. Then last quarter a katar crew walked in with a guard drill and a stack of forged dockets, and the first thing they broke was my schedule. The one thing down there that never broke is why they came. Ask me about that when you've earned the deeper bays.

Wreckers I'd have hired, which is the insulting part. They drill a guard that doesn't give - adamantine, they call it - fists up, feet planted, hours at a stretch, on my power draw. Their foreman files my forms in my own format. Accurate paperwork from thieves. I almost respect it. Almost.

It means whoever holds it holds the bay. That's yard law older than this station's registry. Their copy carries a forged authorization with my stamp on it, and while that flimsi exists, half my subcontractors think the lockout is mine. Bring it back and I start reclaiming my yard one bay at a time.
Six adepts in the Breaker Bay. Bring their work order to my desk in Offices & Labs. A forged stamp is still my problem until I can prove it.
That's junkline grease on your sleeves, and nobody comes back from bay work standing that straight unless the work is done. Flimsi. Desk.

Signed by their foreman, countersigned by nobody, forged stamp and all. I'll file it under evidence and frame the copy. She counts out your pay without looking at it. "Hazard rate, no deductions. That's as warm as I get."

Five specialists have the junkline relay. My shift leads can't move scrap without the crew's say-so now. Go back to the Breaker Bay, beat the five, and pull that relay out of their hands. I'd like to run my own dock again.
The relay comes back in one piece. It bills as salvage, not scrap.

A guard that doesn't break, drilled until it's true. You'd know what that's worth to a katar hand better than I would - I just know what it looks like from a crane cab. My cutters held a plasma lance on one of those adepts for a full minute and he didn't step back. Whatever they're perfecting down there, they didn't invent it. They're drilling it to sell it, and my yard is the free training floor.

That relay is the junkline's spine. Whoever holds it decides where every belt in this yard delivers, and right now that's five squatters with katars and a work ethic I'd kill for. It's also serial-stamped to my yard. Get it back and their reroute becomes theft on paper, which is the only place theft ever really dies.

Because they never work alone and my people do. Every bay they took, they took in pairs and threes - one holds the floor, the rest move the work. It's in my own regs: nobody works a live bay without two spotters. They read my rulebook better than my shift leads do. Learn from that before the deeper bays make you learn it.
Five specialists have the relay in the Breaker Bay. I need the five gone and the junkline controls back.
The belts changed direction an hour ago. I felt it through the deck plating before the sensors bothered telling me, which means you're carrying my relay. Hand it here.

Serial matches. The scorch marks are new, but I'll bill those to their foreman. She logs the relay and your pay in the same motion. "Throughput's already climbing. You're the first line on tomorrow's report. Around here that's a love letter."

The warden holds the Breaker Bay like he's part of the frame. My people can't shift him. Call him out at the challenge marker, beat him, and bring back the sheared bay sigil. Get yourself some spotters before you try it.
Use the Breaker Bay challenge marker to call the warden. My last crew barely got a description of his guard back to me. Beat him, recover the sigil, and do better than that.

He inspects a fight the way I inspect a wreck - finds the load point and plants himself under it. Two of my riggers put a cutting crew's worth of steel into him and his back foot never moved. Understand me: he is not their best. He is their doorman. That's what you're climbing toward, and it's why I said two spotters like I meant it.

The cable snap took that bay off my books before I made foreman. It also left the one thing this yard never managed to break - a bulkhead section that ate the whole whipping cable and didn't dent. That's what drew this crew here. You don't drill an unbreakable guard just anywhere. You drill it in front of the thing that taught it.

Every bay in this yard carries a sigil plate. Cast when the bay is commissioned, pulled when it dies. The sheared bay's plate should have been pulled twenty years ago; their warden wears it like a badge instead. It's my property and my bay's death certificate, and I want it filed properly. Sentiment and paperwork are the same thing if you do them right.
The Breaker Bay challenge marker calls the warden. Beat him and bring me the bay sigil. Take spotters, if you've found any.
You're limping on the left and grinning anyway. That's either a concussion or my sigil in your pack. Show me.

Twenty years overdue and not a corner bent. She sets the sigil on her desk, square to the edge. "First thing I've filed on time all quarter. Your pay is rated for bay-death work - the highest line I sign. Spend it slower than you earned it."

Four foremen still have my override chip. They're authorizing cuts I never signed, and every cut lands on my accounts. Clear the four out of the Breaker Bay and bring me that chip. I'm tired of paying for their training.
Clear the foremen out of the Breaker Bay. If they offer you a contract, remember whose stamp they forged.

The foreman's original crew. The four who walked in with him the first day, back when I still thought they were a salvage bid. Each one has been drilled to hold a bay alone against a full cutting team. They rotate my crane deck in pairs, they sleep in shifts, and they have never once broken my safety regs. Model workers. I want their names off my roster by the weekend.

Used right, nothing - it's a foreman's tool, it makes the yard obey. Used wrong, my stacked hulls come down through the maintenance level and CZ-220 stops having a lower deck. They haven't used it. That's what worries me. People who steal a scalpel and don't cut are waiting for a patient. Get it back before they pick one.

He holds Bay One. The first bay this yard ever commissioned, the one I apprenticed in, and he's turned it into his private drill floor. The crew, the reroute, the chip - all of it is a fence around that one room. He knows I want it back, and he guards it with the only thing in this yard that never breaks. Himself. That bill comes due after the chip.
The four foremen in the Breaker Bay still have my chip. Bring it to my office after you've dealt with them.
The gates started answering my board again mid-shift. Either you have my chip or that crew grew a conscience, and their kind doesn't grow anything. Hand it over.

The chip seats clean. The board is mine again - cranes, gates, belts, all of it. For one second she just breathes, and her shoulders drop half an inch. "That's the yard back. All but one room. Rest up. The last work order I write you is the one I've wanted to write since this started."

The foreman's master is still holding the Breaker Yard. He can stop a cutting crew cold, and I need him off my floor. Use the yard's challenge marker to call him out. Beat him, then come back to my office. I'll count your pay myself.
It's on the clock. Go to the Breaker Yard and use its challenge marker. Keep an eye on his feet. When they finally give ground, finish the job and come back for settlement.

The finished article. Everything his adepts drilled at, he already is. My crane operator swears the load alarm tripped when she swung at him - he caught the wreck ball on crossed blades and the system logged him as a structure. Maybe by now he is one. He came down here to stand in front of the one thing that never breaks, and he stayed until there were two of them. Your job is to put the count back at one.
My yard, and the people who work it. A shift ought to end with everyone still able to go home. That's worth more to me than anything they've pulled out of a wreck.

Then I write the last page. Crew cleared, bays reclaimed, override seated, Bay One recommissioned. A clean file, front to back, and a standing line on my roster with your name on it - rated for anything, paid on time, no questions. Around here that isn't a favor. It's the highest thing I sign.
Call the master at the Breaker Yard's challenge marker. Get him off the floor, then come see me for settlement.

The whole yard went quiet for a second mid-shift. Every belt, every crane, like the place was listening. That was him hitting the deck, wasn't it. Bay One's door is showing open on my board for the first time in twenty years. Get over here.
That's my dock again. Here's your hazard pay, every credit. And if you want Adamantine Guard taught by someone who still knows when to lower it, you've got my attention now.
Back to the work order.
Cut the key. I'll fill the order.
What does this yard actually break?
Whose crew is squatting in your yard?
Why does one flimsi matter that much?
Not this shift.
The Adamantine Guard Breaker Yard Work Order. Filled and pulled.
About the relay job.
Your belts will run the right way by next shift.
What are they actually training down there?
What's one relay worth to you?
How did five people take an entire junkline?
The belts can wait one more shift.
The Adamantine Guard Junkline Control Relay. Careful - it still sparks.
Back to the sheared bay.
I'll find good spotters and challenge the warden.
What makes this warden different?
What happened in the sheared bay?
What's the sigil to you?
Then I'll come back with a crew.
The Adamantine Guard Sheared Bay Sigil. It was on his shoulder.
About the chip.
The chip comes back to your board.
Who are the four?
What happens if they use it?
And their foreman - the one running all this?
Four at once takes planning. Hold the order.
The Adamantine Guard Foreman's Override Chip. Their roster is four names shorter.
Back to Bay One.
I'll get him off your floor.
A week without moving. What is he?
What's in the yard that's worth all this to you?
And after he's down? What then?
Not until my crew is ready. He'll keep.
It's done. His guard broke before he did.
